ARTICLE VIII: GENERAL DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS VIII-33 SECTION 875 – RESIDENTIAL CARE FACILITIES Section 875.01 – Purpose This section is intended, in part, to ensure compliance of related provisions of the Jefferson Township Zoning Resolution with the Fair Housing Act Amendments of 1988, effective March 12, 1989, which extend equal housing opportunities to the handicapped, as well as place some minimal regulations upon residential care facilities in accordance with ORC Chapter 5119. Jefferson Township's policy has been, and shall continue to be, to encourage persons whose disabilities or status limit their ability to live independently, to live in stable, affordable housing, in settings that maximize community integration and opportunities for acceptance and to ensure that these individuals are not forced into housing enclaves that would perpetuate isolation from the mainstream of society.

Small Wind Farms, classified as producing less than 5MW and used as incidental to an agricultural use will be exempt from these zoning regulations in accordance with ORC §519.21. Any proposed construction, erection, or siting of a Small Wind Farm less that 5MW including the wind turbine generator or anemometer or any parts thereof shall be a permitted use in any zoning district except those expressly zoned for residential use. Jefferson Township Parks (“Parks”) are open to the public daily from sunrise to sunset. Except for activities explicitly approved by the Township, all Parks shall be closed from sunset until sunrise. No person may enter, remain upon, or attempt to access any portion of park property while closed. The Township may temporarily close all or portions of a park due to weather, safety, maintenance, or other operational needs. Right-of-Way Guidelines and Requirements Effective: January 26, 2022 Page 36 of 67 4.4.5.1.3 Planting Strip: The space between the curb and the sidewalk is often referred to as the beauty or planting strip. Planting areas that divide lanes of traffic are referred to as median or parkway strips. To accommodate large trees, planting strips should be a minimum of 8 feet wide, for medium sized trees it should be a minimum of 5 feet wide, for small trees it should be a minimum of 4 feet wide (the Acceptable Street Tree List provides a reference column for suitable planter strip size). Trees grown in spaces that are too small will have reduced life spans, develop insect and disease problems, and become stunted by the limited growing space.
